policy_name: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
issuing_authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
regulatory_regime: Voluntary U.S. federal AI risk management guidance (profile of the NIST AI RMF)

locale_context.region: North America › United States (federal, used globally)
locale_context.culture: US standards-body culture: voluntary, consensus-driven, technically grounded and sector-neutral.

key_dates.event: Initial public draft (NIST AI 600-1 ipd) released for comment
Final NIST AI 600-1 published (developed pursuant to EO 14110 Sec. 4.1)
EO 14110, under which the profile was developed, revoked; profile itself not withdrawn
America's AI Action Plan directs revision of the AI RMF; secondary sources report a related revision of AI 600-1 may follow, not published as of Nov 2026

covered_entities: organizations designing, developing, deploying, using or evaluating generative AI (GAI) systems
covered_systems: generative AI systems and models, including foundation / dual-use foundation models
conditions: Voluntary; suggested actions are selected according to the organization's context and risk tolerance
objective: Help organizations identify the unique or exacerbated risks posed by generative AI and propose actions, mapped to the AI RMF subcategories, to govern, map, measure and manage those risks.
conflict_rule: Voluntary and non-binding; suggested actions such as GV-1.1-001 defer to applicable laws and regulations.

sources_consulted: https://huggingface.co/datasets/leeroy-jankins/NIST-GenAI-Profile (copy of the NIST AI 600-1 PDF; PDF metadata author NIST, 64 pp., dated July 2024)
record_provenance.notes: nist.gov hosts could not be fetched from this session; clause text was extracted with pdftotext from a mirror copy of the official PDF hosted on Hugging Face (third-party), whose metadata identifies NIST as author. Re-check against https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1. The profile lists 12 GAI risks (CBRN Information or Capabilities; Confabulation; Dangerous, Violent, or Hateful Content; Data Privacy; Environmental Impacts; Harmful Bias or Homogenization; Human-AI Configuration; Information Integrity; Information Security; Intellectual Property; Obscene, Degrading, and/or Abusive Content; Value Chain and Component Integration). Initial public draft date (29 April 2024) is from general knowledge, not re-verified. Whether NIST will revise AI 600-1 following the July 2025 AI Action Plan is unconfirmed.

clauses.original_text: 1. CBRN Information or Capabilities: Eased access to or synthesis of materially nefarious information or design capabilities related to chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) weapons or other dangerous materials or agents.
clauses.object: CBRN information or capabilities risk from GAI
clauses.requirement: treat eased access to CBRN weapon information/design capabilities as a GAI risk category to be managed
clauses.purpose: prevent GAI uplift to chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapons
clauses.interpretation_notes: Definitional clause from the 12-risk taxonomy; modality is notional (the profile uses the taxonomy to scope suggested actions).

clauses.original_text: Establish minimum thresholds for performance or assurance criteria and review as part of deployment approval (“go/”no-go”) policies, procedures, and processes, with reviewed processes and approval thresholds reflecting measurement of GAI capabilities and risks.
clauses.object: minimum performance/assurance thresholds in go/no-go deployment approval
clauses.requirement: set deployment approval thresholds tied to measured GAI capabilities and risks
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mapped in the profile to CBRN; Confabulation; Dangerous, Violent, or Hateful Content. Quotation marks around go/no-go reproduced as in source.

clauses.original_text: Establish a test plan and response policy, before developing highly capable models, to periodically evaluate whether the model may misuse CBRN information or capabilities and/or offensive cyber capabilities.
clauses.actor: developer of highly capable GAI models
clauses.action: establish test plan and response policy; periodically evaluate
clauses.object: model potential to misuse CBRN or offensive cyber capabilities
clauses.requirement: plan and periodically run dangerous-capability evaluations with a response policy
clauses.purpose: detect and respond to dangerous CBRN/cyber capabilities
clauses.interpretation_notes: 'Highly capable models' is not defined in the profile.

clauses.original_text: Apply established security measures to: Assess likelihood and magnitude of vulnerabilities and threats such as backdoors, compromised dependencies, data breaches, eavesdropping, man-in-the-middle attacks, reverse engineering, autonomous agents, model theft or exposure of model weights, AI inference, bypass, extraction, and other baseline security concerns.
clauses.action: apply security measures and assess vulnerabilities and threats
clauses.requirement: assess likelihood/magnitude of listed security threats including model-weight theft
clauses.purpose: security and resilience of GAI systems
clauses.affected_asset: model weights, training data, system integrity
clauses.interpretation_notes: Mapped to Data Privacy; Information Integrity; Information Security; Value Chain and Component Integration.

clauses.original_text: Establish and regularly review specific criteria that warrants the deactivation of GAI systems in accordance with set risk tolerances and appetites.
clauses.action: establish and regularly review deactivation criteria
clauses.requirement: define and review criteria for deactivating GAI systems
clauses.condition: in accordance with organizational risk tolerances and appetites
clauses.purpose: enable timely shutdown of harmful GAI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Grammar ('criteria that warrants') reproduced as in source.

clauses.original_text: Report GAI incidents in compliance with legal and regulatory requirements (e.g., HIPAA breach reporting, e.g., OCR (2023) or NHTSA (2022) autonomous vehicle crash reporting requirements.
clauses.requirement: report GAI incidents as required by applicable law
clauses.condition: where legal or regulatory reporting requirements apply
clauses.interpretation_notes: Unbalanced parenthesis is in the source. The profile does not itself create a reporting duty; it points to existing legal duties.
